text: This activity explains viewing workflow. Use the viewing system methodically and make a documented, accountable decision. Select each panel to work through the approved practice.

Before viewing begins, confirm that the station is correctly connected and ready: Correct server connection; Correct Viewer ID; Minimum viewing time configured; Appropriate saved palette and default settings. Only a Supervisor may configure the station. Key takeawayThe Viewer confirms readiness; the Supervisor controls configuration.

Press F1 to begin with the Normal image. Examine the full image systematically before concentrating on a particular area. Establishing a baseline helps the Viewer understand where an object sits in relation to the rest of the body. Key takeawayStart with the whole image before examining the detail.

Use zoom, pan or Auto-Pan to move methodically across the image. Do not jump randomly between isolated areas. Systematic examination reduces the chance of overlooking a small, low-contrast object. Key takeawayMethodical viewing is more reliable than random searching.

If an area appears unusual: Adjust brightness and contrast; Examine it at more than one zoom level; Compare Normal, Un-sharp Mask, Emboss, High Contrast and Invert Colours. No single mode is best for every object. Key takeawayNever judge a doubtful area from only one mode or one zoom level.

Use F5 to retrieve a previous image of the same person, where available. Ask: Is the object new?Was it visible before?Has its position or appearance changed?Could it be part of the person rather than a concealed object?Key takeawayComparison adds context to what the Viewer sees today.

Annotate the area and add a concise, factual comment where necessary. Record what was observed without speculation or accusatory language. The annotation should help an authorised Reviewer understand the concern. Key takeawayRecord the observation—not an unsupported conclusion.

state: Step 7: Make and Preserve the Decision
text: After completing the examination, make the authorised decision: Release: No suspicious object requires further action. Hold: Further action or a search is required. The Movement Log preserves the sequence of modes, zooms, pans and adjustments used during the examination. Key takeawayA defensible decision is based on disciplined viewing and a traceable record.

You have reviewed Step 1: Confirm Readiness, Step 2: Begin with Normal View, Step 3: Navigate Systematically, Step 4: Enhance Doubtful Areas. Apply the approved procedure consistently, record what matters and escalate uncertainty rather than improvising.
